terms.definition: An element in Group 18 with a completely full outer shell, making it almost completely unreactive.
terms.function: Stays stable and unreactive because its full shell leaves no need to bond.
terms.whereItIs: Group 18 — the far-right column of the periodic table.
terms.whyItMatters: The noble gases define the 'stability target' that drives all of bonding chemistry.

terms.definition: An outermost electron shell that holds its complete capacity of electrons (2 for the first shell, 8 for the next).
terms.function: Creates the most stable, lowest-energy arrangement an atom can have.
terms.whereItIs: The fully filled ring in the shell-view atom model.
terms.whyItMatters: Other atoms bond specifically to reach this noble-gas-like full-shell state.

terms.definition: A description of substances that almost never take part in chemical reactions.
terms.function: Noble gases are unreactive because they have nothing to gain by bonding.
terms.whereItIs: The reason helium balloons and argon bulbs stay safe and unchanged.
terms.whyItMatters: Unreactivity is what makes noble gases useful in bulbs, balloons, and dive tanks.

terms.definition: The last column of the periodic table, home to helium, neon, argon, krypton, xenon, and radon.
terms.function: Organizes the full-shell family together at the far right of the table.
terms.whereItIs: The glowing last column in the model's table section.
terms.whyItMatters: Every element in this column shares the noble, unreactive personality.
